name: Network by tiers
description: The solution's definition, recorded results and selection first; then its metric and cascade, problems, ideals, queued findings, public evidence and implementations; then its parent briefly, its children and dependencies by purpose, interface and selected arm, and its dependents by what they rely on. A solution with children adds how they combine. Sections fill a budget in tier order and a cut is named.
advantages: Nothing is written per solution; the deciding records (a lost result, a finding) are read first; the budget keeps the closest records when space is short. Selected because: it passes every free case, including those the definition-only baseline misses.
disadvantages: A record that is linked by no column (a finding with no solution or candidate column, a note in prose) is not reached; reading staleness costs a git call per arm.

name: The solution's record alone
description: BASELINE: the solution's own row and nothing connected to it, cut to the budget. It is what a pass reads when no network forms its prompt.
advantages: The smallest prompt; free and instant.
disadvantages: Holds none of the results, findings, parent or children, so it misses every verdict that depends on them.
